ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the incircle $\odot O$ of $\triangle ABC$ is tangent to $AB$, $BC$, $CA$ at points $D$, $E$, and $F$, respectively. If $\angle DEF = 52^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect OD, and OF, \\
$\because$ The incircle $\odot O$ of $\triangle ABC$ is tangent to the sides AB, BC, CA at points D, E, F, respectively,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADO=\angle AFO=90^\circ$；\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A+\angle DOF=180^\circ$，\\
$\because$ $\angle DEF=52^\circ$, and $\angle DOF$ and $\angle DEF$ are the central angle and the inscribed angle subtended by the same arc $\overset{\frown}{DF}$, respectively,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DOF=2\angle DEF=104^\circ$；\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A=180^\circ-\angle DOF=\boxed{76^\circ}$.

Circle O is the incircle of triangle ABC, tangent to AB, BC, and CA at D, E, and F respectively. Points D and F are on the circle and are respectively located on the two oblique sides AB and AC, and point E is on the base BC; in the figure ED and EF are connected, so ∠DEF is an inscribed angle on the circle. Reasoning: ∠DEF = 52°, and what it subtends is the arc DF not containing E, so the corresponding central angle ∠DOF = 2 × 52° = 104°. Because AB and AC are respectively the tangents to the circle at D and F, OD ⟂ AB and OF ⟂ AC, that is, ∠ADO = 90°, ∠AFO = 90°. In quadrilateral ADOF, the sum of the interior angles is 360°, therefore ∠A + ∠DOF + 90° + 90° = 360°. So ∠A = 180° - 104° = 76°.

method.method_draft: From the image, note that D, E, and F are points on the incircle, with E at the bottom tangency and D,F on the two sides meeting at A. The drawn angle ∠DEF is an inscribed angle intercepting the arc DF not containing E. From the text, ∠DEF = 52°. Therefore the corresponding central angle ∠DOF is 2·52° = 104°. Since AB and AC are tangents at D and F, OD ⟂ AB and OF ⟂ AC. In quadrilateral ADOF, the angles at D and F are right angles, so ∠A + ∠DOF = 180°. Hence ∠A = 180° − 104° = 76°.
